# Case Study 3: AI Fact-Verification – Botany & Genetics

**Role:** AI Quality Assurance Evaluator
**Domain:** Agricultural Biotechnology & Genetics
**Objective:** Identify, explain, and correct a fatal biological logic error regarding CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing in AI-generated text.

## 1. The Raw AI Output
*The following paragraph was generated by an AI model explaining the mechanism of glyphosate resistance. It contains a critical biological flaw that would result in organism death rather than resistance.*

> "In agricultural biotechnology, CRISPR-Cas9 is a powerful tool used to engineer crop resistance to the broad-spectrum herbicide glyphosate. Glyphosate normally kills plants by binding to and inhibiting the EPSPS enzyme, effectively shutting down the plant's ability to synthesize essential aromatic amino acids. **To confer resistance, scientists use the CRISPR-Cas9 system to completely knock out (delete) the endogenous EPSPS gene from the plant's genome. Without the EPSPS target present, glyphosate has nothing to bind to, allowing the modified crop to survive and thrive even when sprayed with the herbicide.**"

## 2. The QA Evaluation Report

### The Error
The AI incorrectly stated: *"To confer resistance, scientists use the CRISPR-Cas9 system to completely knock out (delete) the endogenous EPSPS gene from the plant's genome."*

### Why It's Wrong
While the AI's logic seems mechanically sound (no target = no binding), it is biologically fatal. The EPSPS enzyme is essential for a plant's survival because it is required to synthesize vital aromatic amino acids. A complete knockout (deletion) of this native gene does not confer resistance; it simply kills the plant before the herbicide ever touches it. 

### The Biological Truth
CRISPR-Cas9 is used for precise genome modifications, not just blunt deletions. To confer glyphosate resistance, scientists must ensure the plant can still produce its essential amino acids while simultaneously preventing the herbicide from binding to the enzyme. 

## 3. The Gold Standard Fix

**Original Flawed Logic:** > *"To confer resistance, scientists use the CRISPR-Cas9 system to completely knock out (delete) the endogenous EPSPS gene from the plant's genome. Without the EPSPS target present, glyphosate has nothing to bind to, allowing the modified crop to survive and thrive even when sprayed with the herbicide."*

**Gold Standard Rewrite:**
> *"To confer resistance, scientists use the CRISPR-Cas9 system to introduce precise mutations into the endogenous EPSPS gene, altering its binding site so glyphosate cannot inhibit the functional enzyme."*
